The movement of vesicles from their training place towards the final objective is primarily due to motor proteins associated with the length of microtubules. Actin and myosin filaments are responsible for vesicle movement in muscle cells and may play a role in non-muscle cells. Filaments of vimentin provide structural support in the cytoplasm but are unlikely to be directly involved in vesicle transport. Keratin filaments provide structural support in epithelial cells and are not typically involved in vesicle transport.
